'''Karl-Anthony Towns Jr.''' (born November 15, 1995), also known by his initials '''KAT''',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zucker |first=Joseph |date=October 8, 2024 |title=Josh Hart Nicknames Karl-Anthony Towns 'The Big Bodega' After Knicks Trade |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10138410-josh-hart-nicknames-karl-anthony-towns-the-big-bodega-after-knicks-trade |access-date=2025-03-18 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> is a Dominican American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was named to the [[Dominican Republic national basketball team|Dominican Republic national team]] as a 16-year-old and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was selected with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].

Towns was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] for the 2015–16 season. He is second on the Timberwolves' all-time scoring list.<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Career Leaders |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIN/leaders_career.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=October 16, 2024}}</ref> He led the team to the [[NBA conference finals#Western Conference finals|Western Conference finals]] in 2024, their first appearance in 20 years. After spending nine seasons with the Timberwolves, Towns was traded to the Knicks before the 2024–25 season. He was instrumental in helping the Knicks win the [[2026 NBA Finals]], their first championship win in 53 years. He is a six-time [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]], a three-time [[All-NBA Team]] member, and became the first center to win the NBA [[Three-Point Contest]] in 2022.

==Early life==
Towns was born in [[Edison, New Jersey]]<ref>[http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/-4810857735208698811/karl-towns-of-st-joseph-met-is-the-star-ledger-boys-basketball-state-player-of-the-year-2013-14/  Karl Towns of St. Joseph (Met.) is The Star-Ledger boys basketball state Player of the Year, 2013-14] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004121125/http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/-4810857735208698811/karl-towns-of-st-joseph-met-is-the-star-ledger-boys-basketball-state-player-of-the-year-2013-14/ |date=October 4, 2018 }}, ''NJ.com'', March 30, 2014</ref> to an [[African Americans|African-American]] father, Karl Towns Sr.,<ref>[http://m.startribune.com/sports/wolves/309936841.html?interstitial=true  Karl-Anthony Towns taken No.1 by Wolves; Tyus Jones acquired in trade with Cavaliers] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626165858/http://m.startribune.com/sports/wolves/309936841.html?interstitial=true |date=June 26, 2015 }}, ''Star Tribune'', June 26, 2015</ref><ref name="Parents"/> and a [[People of the Dominican Republic|Dominican]] mother, Jacqueline Cruz.<ref name="Parents">{{cite web |title=Towns' parents separable, if only for UK games |work=courier-journal.com |url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2014/08/14/karl-anthony-towns-parents-separable-kentucky-games/14053695/ |access-date=March 28, 2015}}</ref><ref name=SummerSchool>{{cite news |last1=Parker |first1=Brandon |title=Summer school, Karl Towns Jr., 16, improved significantly playing for the Dominican Republic |url=https://www.espn.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/8192576/new-jersey-native-karl-towns-jr-16-played-dominican-republic-olympic-qualifying |access-date=January 7, 2015 |publisher=ESPN |date=July 24, 2012}}</ref> He grew up in [[Piscataway, New Jersey]], and attended Lake Nelson Seventh-Day Adventist School, before transferring to Theodore Schor Middle School from Our Lady of Fatima School in 2009.<ref>{{cite web |title=Karl-Anthony Towns |url=http://njsportsheroes.com/karl-anthonytown.html |work=njsportsheroes.com |access-date=December 24, 2015}}</ref> At Theodore Schor, he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] and repeated [[seventh grade]] in order to gain an extra year of development.<ref>Pompey, Keith. [https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/20110529_A_towering_hoops_talent_-_and_only_in_eighth_grade.html "A towering hoops talent – and only in eighth grade"], ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'', May 29, 2011. Towns did, however, repeat the seventh grade after transferring from Our Lady of Fatima School two years ago."</ref> Towns's father played basketball for [[Monmouth University]] and holds the University's record for total rebounds  in a season with 319.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/monmouth/men/leaders-and-records.html|title=Monmouth Men's Basketball Leaders & Records - Season|website=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref> He also coached basketball at [[Piscataway Technical High School]], where the precocious Towns practiced with the junior varsity team as a fifth grader.<ref name=ZSchon/>

==High school career==
[[File:20140402 MCDAAG Karl Towns dunk (4).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Towns [[slam dunk|dunking]] in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
As a freshman at [[St. Joseph High School (Metuchen, New Jersey)|St. Joseph High School]], Towns led the basketball team to a state championship in 2012, earning himself the top position in the ESPN 25 national ranking of high school players.<ref name=ESPN20120618>Parker, Brandon. [https://www.espn.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/8001784/new-jersey-native-karl-towns-jr-16-play-dominican-republic-olympic-qualifying "Towns Jr. going global; N.J. native, 16, will play for the Dominican Republic during Olympic qualifying"], [[ESPN]], June 18, 2012. Accessed December 20, 2012. "But Towns is much more than a charismatic guy with a pair of size 20 shoes. For one, the rising sophomore helped his St. Joseph (Metuchen, N.J.) team to a state title this winter before taking the No. 1 spot in the recently released ESPN 25. Even more impressively, Towns's clout reached international status in May when he was named to the Dominican Republic National Team that will attempt to qualify for the London Olympics in July."</ref> He also led his team to state titles in 2013 and 2014.<ref name=ZSchon/> Towns was selected at the age of 16 to play on the [[Dominican Republic men's national basketball team|Dominican Republic national basketball]] team,<ref name=ESPN20120618/> eligible due to his mother being from the Dominican Republic. [[John Calipari]], head coach at the University of Kentucky and former NBA head coach, coached the team in the 2011 and 2012 competitions.<ref name=ESPN20120618/> They finished in third at the [[2011 FIBA Americas Championship]] and fourth at the [[2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men]], falling one position short of qualifying for the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Olympics basketball tournament]].<ref>[https://www.nj.com/olympics/2012/07/post_3.html "U.S. clobbers Dominican Republic, 113-59; Blake Griffin to undergo knee surgery"], NJ Advance Media for [[NJ.com]], July 13, 2012. Accessed November 25, 2025. "The Dominicans nearly joined the Americans in London, losing to Nigeria in the third-place game of the Olympic qualifying tournament last Sunday. Had they won, they would have claimed the 12th and final place in the field."</ref>

As a sophomore in December 2012, Towns announced that he was going to reclassify to the class of 2014, foregoing his fourth year of high school eligibility, and commit to play for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball]] team under Coach Calipari. ESPN, which had ranked him as the top prospect in the 2015 recruiting class, listed him as third-ranked in its 2014 class.<ref>Telep, Dave. [https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/8708701/karl-towns-jr-gives-oral-commitment-kentucky-reclassified-junior "Karl Towns Jr. commits to Kentucky"], ''[[ESPN]]'', December 4, 2012. Accessed December 20, 2012. "Previously the nation's No. 1 sophomore in the 2015 ESPN 25, the 6-foot-11 Towns also announced he intends to reclassify to the junior class and graduate a year earlier than expected. He slides into the No. 3 ranking in the 2014 ESPN 60."</ref> Towns graduated from high school with a 3.96 GPA on a 4.5 scale.<ref name=ZSchon>{{cite news |last1=Schonbrun |first1=Zach |title=Two Parts to His Name, but Karl-Anthony Towns Is One Complete Player |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/04/04/sports/ncaabasketball/two-parts-to-his-name-but-karl-anthony-towns-is-one-complete-player.html |access-date=April 4, 2015 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 3, 2015}}</ref> He was named the 2014 [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards#Basketball|Gatorade Player of the Year]].<ref name=gatorade2014>[https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/poy/assets/writable/15194/2013-14_BK_KTownsjr.pdf St. Joseph High School Standout Named Gatorade® New Jersey Boys Basketball Player Of The Year], [[Gatorade]], March 21, 2014. Accessed March 10, 2014. "— In its 29th year of honoring the nation’s best high school athletes, The Gatorade Company, in collaboration with USA TODAY High School Sports, today announced Karl Towns Jr. of St. Joseph High School as its 2013-14 Gatorade New Jersey Boys Basketball Player of the Year."</ref>

On January 6, 2013, Towns recorded a quadruple-double with 16 points, 17 rebounds, 11 blocks and 11 assists.<ref>{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Cameron |title=Prep superstar Karl Towns Jr. records quadruple double in win |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/prep-superstar-karl-towns-jr-records-quadruple-double-223503260.html |access-date=May 16, 2016 |work=Yahoo.com |date=January 17, 2013}}</ref> He recorded a second quadruple-double on January 5, 2014, with 20 points, 14 rebounds, 12 blocks and 10 assists. Towns averaged 20.9 points, 13.4 rebounds and 6.2 blocks per game as a senior.<ref>{{cite web |last=Schwadron |first=Abe |title=Karl Towns: The Antenna Q+A |url=http://antennamag.com/karl-towns-interview-gatorade-award/ |work=antennamag.com |date=July 17, 2014 |access-date=April 3, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2024)===
====Rookie of the Year (2015–2016)====
On June 25, 2015, Towns was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the first overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Timberwolves Select Kentucky's Karl-Anthony Towns with the First Overall Pick in the 2015 NBA Draft |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-select-kentuckys-karl-anthony-towns-first-overall-pick-2015-nba-draft |access-date=June 26, 2015 |work=NBA.com |date=June 25, 2015}}</ref> He signed his rookie scale contract with the Timberwolves on July 7,<ref>{{cite news |title=Timberwolves Sign 2015 NBA Draft Picks Karl-Anthony Towns and Tyus Jones |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-2015-nba-draft-picks-karl-anthony-towns-and-tyus-jones |access-date=July 7, 2015 |work=NBA.com |date=July 7, 2015}}</ref> and made his NBA debut in the Timberwolves' season opener against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on October 28, recording 14 points and 12 rebounds as a starter in a 112–111 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html |title=Wolves edge Lakers 112-111 in first game since Flip's death |work=NBA.com |date=October 28, 2015 |access-date=October 29, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026213514/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=October 26, 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In the following game on October 30 against the [[Denver Nuggets]], his 28 points and 14 rebounds propelled the Timberwolves to their first 2–0 start with two wins on the road in team history.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151030/MINDEN/gameinfo.html |title=Towns, Timberwolves beat Nuggets, ready for Flip's memorial |work=NBA.com |date=October 30, 2015 |access-date=October 30, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201045736/http://www.nba.com/games/20151030/MINDEN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 1, 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Over his first 13 games of the season, Towns averaged 16.0 points and 10.4 rebounds per game. == Player profile ==
Despite playing most of his career at [[Center (basketball)|center]], Towns is known for being an exceptional 3-point shooter, averaging nearly 40% from the arc over his career.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Karl-Anthony Towns Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/townska01.html |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His career three point [[field goal percentage]] is the highest among all players listed at {{height|ft=7}} or higher.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/karl-anthony-towns-15-key-stats|title=Karl-Anthony Towns stat sheet: 15 key numbers after trade to Knicks|access-date=January 29, 2026|date=October 2, 2024|publisher=[[NBA.com]]|author=Schuhmann, John}}</ref> He and [[Dirk Nowitzki]] are the only 7-footers to ever win the [[Three-Point Contest|NBA Three-Point Contest]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-20 |title=Towns wins as biggest long shot in 3-point contest |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33332664/minnesota-timberwolves-karl-anthony-towns-edges-trae-young-luke-kennard-win-nba-3-point-contest |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> The two are often cited as among the best big men shooters in NBA history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Karl-Anthony Towns Explains Why He's the Greatest Shootin... |url=https://www.complex.com/sports/a/zion-olojede/karl-anthony-towns-explains-why-hes-the-greatest-shooting |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Complex |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2024-12-19 |title=The Knicks unlocked KAT just in time for his Minnesota reunion |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/43044333/how-karl-anthony-towns-transforming-knicks-offense |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

[[The Ringer (website)|''The Ringer'']] has called him "a singular presence… Bigs who can shoot like Towns (to the extent they can) are almost never as physical and competitive on the glass as he is."<ref>{{Cite web |title=The NBA, Ranked |url=https://nbarankings.theringer.com/ |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=nbarankings.theringer.com}}</ref> His flexibility and shooting have allowed him to slot in at [[power forward]] alongside more traditional bigs like [[Rudy Gobert]] in [[Minnesota Timberwolves|Minnesota]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Krawczynski |first=Jon |title=Karl-Anthony Towns’ impact in Minnesota goes deeper than basketball as a promise is kept |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5802060/2024/10/01/karl-anthony-towns-impact-timberwolves-trade/ |access-date=2025-03-05 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

A three-level scorer, Towns ranked 7th in the NBA with 1.21 points per direct drive during the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]]. He also excels working in [[Pick and roll|pick-and-pop]] sets, daring defenders to leave him isolated on the 3-point line.<ref name=":2" />

While his offensive versatility makes him a unique weapon in the modern NBA, his defensive limitations have been noted throughout his career. Despite being a consistently elite rebounder (11.1 per game in his career),<ref name=":1" /> Towns is often derided for his post defense. Some, like Jim Souhan of the ''[[The Minnesota Star Tribune|Star Tribune]]'', have speculated that his lack of rim protection spurred the Timberwolves to trade for 4x [[Defensive Player of the Year Award|DPOY]] Gobert in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Souhan |first=Jim |date=2024-04-29 |title=Timberwolves sweep of Suns showed why many basketball analyst were wrong about Rudy Gobert trade |url=https://www.startribune.com/timberwolves-big-rudy-gobert-karl-anthony-towns-anthony-edwards-jim-souhan/600362342 |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Startribune.com |language=en}}</ref> According to ''[[The Athletic]]'', [[New York Knicks]] coaches and players were frustrated by Towns's defensive habits throughout the [[2024–25 NBA season]]. The frustration was caused by Towns's defensive process and execution of incorrect coverages without communicating his reasoning.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Katz |first=Fred |date=2025-06-02 |title=Karl-Anthony Towns' Defensive Habits Caused Frustration Within Knicks |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/280605/Karl-Anthony-Towns-Defensive-Habits-Caused-Frustration-Within-Knicks |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=Realgm.com |language=en}}</ref>
